newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's 1996 public debt rose to 69.3 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Spain's 1996 public debt rose to 69.3 pct of GDP.

text.p: Spanish public debt rose four percentage points in 1996 to represent 69.3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said on Wednesday.
"At the end of 1996, public debt reached 69.3 percent which was a rise of four points over GDP versus 1995," Montoro told a parliamentary committee.
Montoro said the increase in public debt was due to several factors.
These included "growth of debt issues of more than was initially forecast, due to the need to finance the budget hole discovered in July," he said.

Interest rate cuts in the latter part of 1996 "called for the Treasury to redirect the financing forecast for foreign currencies over to peseta issues," which implied an increase in public debt of 35 billion pesetas.
Montoro added that debt taken on by the State for several public entities swelled public debt by a further 450 billion pesetas.
